question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (open-ended Cat III AIF) is declaring First Close. It has received capital commitments of INR 18 crore from anchor investors plus INR 2 crore sponsor contribution. Can it validly declare First Close?

answer.text: Yes; the INR 20 crore total (commitments + sponsor) meets SEBI's minimum corpus requirement at First Close
Yes; any corpus amount is permitted at First Close for open-ended Cat III AIFs
No; the minimum corpus requirement at First Close is INR 50 crore
No; sponsor contribution cannot be counted toward First Close corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI requires that the corpus of any AIF at First Close shall NOT be less than INR 20 crore. The corpus includes committed capital from investors AND sponsor commitment, which is itself an investment in the scheme. INR 18 crore + INR 2 crore = INR 20 crore, which exactly meets the threshold. The Trap: Option B ignores the INR 20 crore floor altogether. Option C inflates the floor to INR 50 crore. Option D wrongly excludes sponsor contribution, which must be made through scheme investment and does count toward corpus. Note: Once First Close is declared, the sponsor commitment cannot be reduced, withdrawn, or transferred during the life of the fund.
